evidence: Liv. praef. 10: inde foedum inceptū foedum exitū quod vītēs
Publ. I 20: Īrātum breviter vītēs, inimīcum diū.

terms.gloss: avoid, get out of the way of
evidence: Cic. Amic. 88: quās tum ēvītāre, tum ēlevāre, tum ferre sapientis est
Traupman 97, 307: rem ēvītāre, to duck the issue

terms.gloss: turn aside from, steer clear of
terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation; with an accusative, or ab and the ablative
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.145: ab iīs est dīligentius dēclīnandum
Publ. I 43: Inertia indicātur, cum fugitur labor.

terms.gloss: beware of, take care not to
terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation; with an accusative, or nē and the subjunctive
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.123: nihil autem magis cavendum est senectūtī, quam nē languōrī sē dēsidiaeque dēdat
terms.comment: To avoid doing something is cavē nē with the subjunctive, or cavē with the subjunctive alone. See careful, don’t fall.

phrases.latin: inde tibi tuaeque reī pūblicae quod imitēre capiās, inde foedum inceptū foedum exitū quod vītēs
phrases.english: From it you may take for yourself and your country what to imitate, and from it what to avoid, foul in its beginning, foul in its end.

phrases.latin: ferās, nōn culpēs, quod vītārī nōn potest
phrases.english: What cannot be avoided you must bear, not blame.

phrases.latin: est enim varius et multiplex ūsus amīcitiae multaeque causae suspīciōnum offēnsiōnumque dantur, quās tum ēvītāre, tum ēlevāre, tum ferre sapientis est
phrases.english: For friendship has many uses and many sides, and many causes of suspicion and offence arise, which it is the wise man’s part now to avoid, now to make light of, now to bear.
